Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 1) Which of the following is the most abundant protein in the human body?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Collagen is the principal structural protein of connective tissue and accounts for nearly one-third of total body protein.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 2) The major function of plasma albumin is to:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Albumin contributes most of the plasma oncotic pressure and also serves as a carrier for many endogenous and exogenous substances.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 3) Which lipoprotein is responsible for transporting dietary triglycerides from the intestine?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Chylomicrons are formed in intestinal mucosal cells and carry absorbed dietary triglycerides to peripheral tissues.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 4) The lipoprotein primarily responsible for reverse cholesterol transport is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: HDL removes excess cholesterol from peripheral tissues and transports it back to the liver for disposal.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 5) A 45-year-old man is admitted with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back. Laboratory tests suggest acute pancreatitis. Which enzyme is most specific for confirming the diagnosis?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Both amylase and lipase may rise in acute pancreatitis, but lipase remains elevated longer and is more specific for pancreatic injury.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 6) The structural unit of a protein is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Proteins are polymers formed by linking amino acids through peptide bonds.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 7) The bond that joins two amino acids together is called:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: A peptide bond forms between the amino group of one amino acid and the carboxyl group of another.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 8) Which amino acid contains sulfur?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Methionine is a sulfur-containing essential amino acid and serves as an important methyl group donor.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 9) The α-helix is an example of which level of protein structure?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Hydrogen bonds stabilize the α-helix and β-pleated sheet, which together constitute the secondary structure of proteins.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 10) Denaturation of a protein primarily affects its:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Denaturation disrupts the three-dimensional configuration of proteins without breaking peptide bonds.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 11) The simplest amino acid is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Glycine has a hydrogen atom as its side chain, making it the smallest amino acid.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 12) Which amino acid contains an aromatic ring?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Phenylalanine is an aromatic essential amino acid and serves as a precursor of tyrosine.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 13) The protein responsible for maintaining the elasticity of connective tissue is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Elastin allows tissues such as lungs, arteries and skin to stretch and recoil.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 14) Which protein is the major component of hair and nails?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Keratin is a fibrous structural protein that provides strength to hair, nails and the outer layer of skin.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 15) Which of the following is a simple protein?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Simple proteins yield only amino acids upon hydrolysis, whereas conjugated proteins contain an additional prosthetic group.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 16) The enzyme that catalyzes a biochemical reaction without being consumed is known as a:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Enzymes are biological catalysts that increase reaction rates while remaining chemically unchanged.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 17) The non-protein part essential for the activity of certain enzymes is called:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Coenzymes are usually organic molecules, many of which are derived from vitamins, that assist enzyme function.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 18) An inactive enzyme lacking its required cofactor is called:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: An apoenzyme becomes catalytically active only after combining with its required cofactor.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 19) The complete, catalytically active form of an enzyme is called:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: A holoenzyme consists of the apoenzyme together with its necessary cofactor or coenzyme.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 20) Which vitamin serves as a precursor of NAD⁺ and NADP⁺?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Niacin gives rise to NAD⁺ and NADP⁺, two essential coenzymes involved in oxidation-reduction reactions.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 21) An enzyme that exists in different molecular forms but catalyzes the same reaction is called a(n):
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Isoenzymes differ in structure and tissue distribution while performing the same catalytic function.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 22) Which isoenzyme is most useful in confirming acute myocardial infarction in classical enzyme testing?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: CK-MB is concentrated in cardiac muscle and rises following myocardial injury, making it a useful cardiac marker.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 23) Lactose is composed of:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Lactose, the principal sugar of milk, consists of one molecule each of glucose and galactose.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 24) Maltose is formed by the combination of:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Maltose is produced during starch digestion and is composed of two glucose molecules.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 25) Which polysaccharide is the principal storage carbohydrate in plants?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Plants store excess glucose in the form of starch, whereas animals store it as glycogen.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 26) Which lipid is the major constituent of cell membranes?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Phospholipids form the structural bilayer of biological membranes and help regulate membrane fluidity.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 27) The immediate precursor of steroid hormones is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Cholesterol serves as the parent molecule for steroid hormones, bile acids and vitamin D.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 28) A patient develops generalized edema due to severe protein deficiency. Which plasma protein is most likely reduced?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Reduced albumin lowers plasma oncotic pressure, allowing fluid to shift into the interstitial space and produce edema.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 29) Which of the following is a phosphoprotein?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Casein, the major protein in milk, contains phosphate groups and is classified as a phosphoprotein.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 30) A laboratory report shows elevated CK-MB with typical chest pain and ECG changes. The most likely diagnosis is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: A rise in CK-MB in the appropriate clinical setting strongly suggests injury to cardiac muscle, particularly acute myocardial infarction.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 31) Which plasma protein plays the greatest role in transporting free fatty acids?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Besides maintaining oncotic pressure, albumin serves as the major carrier of free fatty acids, bilirubin, calcium, and many drugs.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 32) Which of the following amino acids contains an imino group?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Proline has a unique cyclic structure with an imino group, influencing protein folding.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 33) The strongest chemical bond stabilizing the primary structure of a protein is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: The primary structure is the linear sequence of amino acids held together by peptide bonds.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 34) Which amino acid is the precursor of serotonin?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Tryptophan is converted into serotonin and subsequently into melatonin.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 35) Histamine is synthesized from:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Histidine undergoes decarboxylation to form histamine, an important inflammatory mediator.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 36) Tyrosine is the precursor of all except:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Serotonin is derived from tryptophan, whereas tyrosine gives rise to catecholamines, melanin, and thyroid hormones.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 37) The amino acid absent from collagen is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Collagen is rich in glycine, hydroxyproline, and hydroxylysine but lacks tryptophan.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 38) Which vitamin is required for hydroxylation of proline during collagen synthesis?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Vitamin C is essential for normal collagen formation; deficiency leads to defective connective tissue.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 39) A deficiency of vitamin C primarily affects the synthesis of:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Impaired collagen formation causes bleeding gums, poor wound healing, and fragile blood vessels.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 40) Which protein is mainly responsible for blood clot formation?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Fibrinogen is converted into fibrin, which forms the structural framework of a blood clot.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 41) The building blocks of nucleic acids are:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: DNA and RNA are polymers made up of repeating nucleotide units.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 42) Each nucleotide consists of:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: These three components combine to form the basic structural unit of nucleic acids.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 43) Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA but absent in DNA?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: RNA contains uracil in place of thymine, which is found in DNA.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 44) The sugar present in DNA is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: DNA contains deoxyribose, whereas RNA contains ribose.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 45) Which of the following is a pyrimidine base?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Cytosine, thymine, and uracil are pyrimidines, while adenine and guanine are purines.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 46) The major storage form of fat in the body is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Triglycerides stored in adipose tissue serve as the body’s main energy reserve.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 47) Which fatty acid is considered essential in humans?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Essential fatty acids cannot be synthesized by the body and must be supplied through the diet.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 48) The predominant fatty acid in olive oil is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Olive oil is rich in monounsaturated oleic acid, which is considered heart-friendly.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 49) Phospholipids are essential components of:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: The phospholipid bilayer forms the basic structural framework of all biological membranes.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 50) Which lipoprotein contains the highest proportion of protein?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: HDL has the greatest protein content, making it the densest of all lipoproteins.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 51) A patient with severe liver disease develops generalized edema. The edema is mainly due to reduced synthesis of:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: The liver synthesizes albumin. Reduced production lowers plasma oncotic pressure, allowing fluid to accumulate in tissues.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 52) Which enzyme hydrolyzes triglycerides into glycerol and fatty acids?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Lipase specifically digests triglycerides and is essential for fat digestion.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 53) Which enzyme is present in saliva?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Salivary amylase initiates starch digestion in the oral cavity before food reaches the stomach.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 54) Enzymes accelerate biochemical reactions by:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.option1: Becoming part of the final product
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Lowering activation energy allows reactions to proceed more rapidly without altering the reaction equilibrium.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 55) A child has bleeding gums, delayed wound healing, and easy bruising. The biochemical defect primarily involves impaired synthesis of:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: These classic features are due to defective collagen formation resulting from inadequate hydroxylation of collagen fibers.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 56) The principal carbohydrate present in milk is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Lactose is the characteristic sugar of milk and serves as an important energy source during infancy.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 57) The sweetest naturally occurring sugar is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Fructose has the highest sweetening power among the naturally occurring sugars.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 58) Which polysaccharide is completely indigestible by humans?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Humans lack the enzyme cellulase, so cellulose functions as dietary fiber.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 59) The major storage site of glycogen in the body is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: The liver maintains blood glucose, while skeletal muscle glycogen serves as a local energy reserve.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 60) Which carbohydrate is commonly known as grape sugar?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Glucose occurs abundantly in grapes and is the principal circulating sugar in human blood.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 61) The basic unit of starch is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Starch consists of repeating glucose molecules arranged as amylose and amylopectin.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 62) Which of the following is a monosaccharide?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Monosaccharides are single sugar units that cannot be hydrolyzed into simpler carbohydrates.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 63) The major function of triglycerides in the body is:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Triglycerides provide the largest energy reserve and also help insulate the body.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 64) Which lipid acts as the precursor of bile acids?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Cholesterol is converted in the liver into bile acids, which aid fat digestion.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 65) A coenzyme is best described as:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.option2: An organic molecule required for enzyme activity
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Most coenzymes are vitamin derivatives that assist enzymes during biochemical reactions.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 66) Which of the following acts as a cofactor for many enzymes?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Magnesium is an essential metal ion that activates numerous enzymes involved in ATP-dependent reactions.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 67) Enzymes are chemically classified as:
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Almost all enzymes are proteins, with the exception of a few catalytic RNA molecules.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 68) Which property is characteristic of enzymes?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.option2: They function equally at all temperatures.
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Most enzymes act on specific substrates because of the precise configuration of their active sites.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 69) Which plasma lipoprotein is commonly referred to as “bad cholesterol”?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Elevated LDL promotes cholesterol deposition in arterial walls, increasing the risk of atherosclerosis.

Biophysics & Biomolecules.question: 70) A patient has markedly elevated LDL cholesterol but normal HDL levels. Which long-term complication is he most likely to develop?
Biophysics & Biomolecules.exp: Persistently high LDL accelerates atherosclerotic plaque formation, predisposing to coronary artery disease and stroke.
